messages.content: We are looking at New Orleans for the January school holiday weekend, Friday the 16th through Monday the 19th. It would be the three of us. I need to decide whether it makes more sense to drive from Dallas after our daughter gets out of school Friday or fly down Saturday morning.
What times are the two activities you are trying to protect? That will determine whether a Saturday flight is genuinely workable rather than just shorter on paper.
The family printmaking program at the Contemporary Arts Center starts at 1:00 Saturday. On Sunday we want the aquarium at 2:00. We have not paid for either yet.

A Saturday nonstop can work if it leaves DFW by about 7:30 a.m. A representative schedule is 7:05-8:32 a.m. Allowing 35 minutes from landing to the curb and roughly 25 minutes into the city, you should reach a Warehouse District hotel around 9:30-9:45. Even if the room is not ready, you could leave luggage and have more than two hours before the printmaking program. Door to door, though, that means leaving home around 4:45 a.m. Driving Friday is about 510 miles and typically 8 hours 15 minutes without stops; with dinner, fuel, and holiday traffic, I would budget 9 to 9.5 hours. A 4:15 p.m. departure puts you at the hotel around 1:15-1:45 a.m.
Compare the actual cost, including the pieces people tend to leave out. We would come home Monday afternoon either way.

For flying, current planning fares for three nonstop round trips are about $804 total. Add roughly $95 for rides between home and DFW, $90 for airport transfers in New Orleans, and about $45 for local rides if you stay outside the Warehouse District: $1,034 before lodging. A Warehouse District stay could reduce the local rides to around $20, making transportation about $1,009. For driving, 1,020 round-trip miles at 25 mpg and $3.05 per gallon is about $125 in fuel. Add $18 in tolls, about $35 for a meal and snacks on the road, and three nights of parking. Parking is the swing item: approximately $90 at a streetcar-line hotel or $150-$165 in the Warehouse District or near the Quarter. That makes driving transportation roughly $268-$343. It saves about $675-$740, but costs most of Friday evening and Monday's daylight.
That is a bigger gap than I expected. What hotel areas would you consider? I do not want us in a room with one bed and a pullout unless there is no reasonable alternative.

I would compare three zones. The Warehouse District is easiest for Saturday: the CAC is a short walk, and the aquarium is about a 15-minute walk or brief ride. Two-queen rooms are common, but rates and parking are higher. The Canal Street edge of the French Quarter gives you good access to the aquarium and restaurants, while the CAC is about 15-20 minutes on foot; noise varies by block and valet parking is usually expensive. Along St. Charles Avenue in the Garden District, rates and parking can be lower and two-queen rooms are available, but the streetcar is slow enough that I would allow 30-40 minutes to reach either activity on a holiday weekend.
Give me one realistic hotel in each area, with the full three-night number for two queens. We are not looking for luxury.

Using refundable planning rates and including estimated hotel taxes: Hotel Fontenot in the Warehouse District is about $846 for three nights in a room with two queen beds. Valet parking is approximately $52 nightly, so the drive-in total would be about $1,002. The Hampton Inn & Suites French Quarter Area on Carondelet, just outside the Quarter, is about $792 with two queens and breakfast; valet is approximately $48 nightly, bringing it to $936 if you drive. The Hampton Inn on St. Charles in the Garden District is about $738 with two queens and breakfast; estimated parking is $30 nightly, or $828 with a car. Exact inventory and cancellation deadlines need live verification before purchase.
The Carondelet one sounds like it might be the middle ground. Is it actually convenient to both places, or does the map make it look better than it is?

It is a legitimate middle ground. It is roughly 0.8 mile to the CAC, about an 18-minute walk, and around 0.9 mile to the aquarium. The aquarium route is straightforward toward the river. For Saturday, you could walk to the CAC if the weather is good or take a short ride. The immediate block is busier than the Garden District but not deep in the Bourbon Street nightlife corridor. Its main drawbacks are valet cost if you drive and occasional street noise, so requesting a room away from the street would matter for this stay.
Now put the two sensible combinations side by side. I think those are driving with the St. Charles hotel and flying with either Carondelet or the Warehouse District.

Driving plus the St. Charles hotel is approximately $1,096: $828 for room and parking, $125 fuel, $18 tolls, $35 road food, and about $90 for three days of streetcar fares and occasional rides. Flying plus Carondelet is approximately $1,851: $792 lodging, $804 airfare, $95 Dallas airport rides, $90 New Orleans airport transfers, and about $70 for local rides and transit. Flying plus Hotel Fontenot is about $1,870: $846 lodging, the same $989 for airfare and airport transfers, and roughly $35 for local transportation because both activities are close. The two flying options are nearly even; Fontenot buys the simplest Saturday, while Carondelet includes breakfast and is a little better positioned for exploring the Quarter.
Add the activities and a realistic food allowance. The printmaking program is $18 each. Use regular aquarium admission, not any package.

The printmaking program is $54 for three. Regular aquarium admission is approximately $40 per adult and $30 for a youth ticket, so I would hold $110 plus about $10 for fees, or $120 total. For food, $390 is a workable allowance: three breakfasts are covered at either Hampton, then budget two lunches, three dinners, snacks, and Monday breakfast or brunch. At Fontenot, where breakfast is not included, I would use $455. That produces complete planning totals of about $1,660 for driving plus St. Charles, $2,415 for flying plus Carondelet, and $2,499 for flying plus Fontenot. Souvenirs are excluded.
Wait, if we drive Friday and arrive after one in the morning, is the hotel definitely going to keep the room? I do not want the reservation treated as a no-show.

A guaranteed reservation should be held, but an arrival after midnight needs direct handling because the property may run its nightly audit before you reach it. The reservation should show arrival on Friday the 16th, not Saturday, and the hotel should be called that afternoon with an estimated arrival around 1:30 a.m. Ask the desk to add a late-arrival note and confirm that the room will not be released. Keep the confirmation number and the name of the employee who acknowledges it.
I am also thinking about Monday. If we leave New Orleans around 2:30 after lunch, when are we realistically home?

With one fuel stop, a meal or longer rest break, and normal traffic entering Dallas, plan on 9 to 9.5 hours. Leaving at 2:30 p.m. puts you home around 11:30 p.m. to midnight. A holiday-weekend traffic delay could push that later. By comparison, a nonstop around 4:30 p.m. would require leaving the hotel near 2:00, land at DFW around 6:00, and likely put you home between 7:15 and 7:45 p.m.
That changes it. She has school Tuesday, and midnight is too late. Is there an earlier driving departure that does not waste the whole Monday?

Leaving by 11:00 a.m. is the practical compromise. You could have breakfast, take a short walk, check out, and be home around 8:00-8:30 p.m. Leaving at noon moves arrival closer to 9:30. You would still have Friday night in transit and give up Monday afternoon, but the trip remains about $755 less than flying with Carondelet.

Between the two flying hotels, take Fontenot out. Breakfast and being between the Quarter and the activities are more useful than saving a few rides. Check whether the Saturday morning flight still leaves enough margin if it runs an hour late.

With a one-hour delay, the 7:05 flight would land around 9:32. A conservative curb time of 10:15 and a 30-minute transfer would put you at Carondelet around 10:45. After leaving bags, you could depart the hotel by 11:30 and reach the CAC around noon, leaving about an hour before the 1:00 program. A delay approaching two hours would make the margin uncomfortable, but a one-hour delay is manageable. The safer backup is to use a ride to the CAC and arrange early bag drop with the hotel in advance.
Then narrow it to the Saturday flight and the Carondelet Hampton. Do not book anything yet. Give me the exact working budget and what still needs confirmation.

The working choice is a Saturday morning nonstop from DFW, returning Monday around 4:30 p.m., with three nights at the Hampton Inn & Suites on Carondelet in a two-queen room. Planning budget: $804 airfare, $792 hotel with taxes, $95 Dallas airport rides, $90 New Orleans airport transfers, $70 local transportation, $54 printmaking, $120 aquarium admission and fees, and $390 for food. Total: $2,415 for three people. Before booking, verify live flight prices and change terms, confirm that the hotel rate is refundable and specifically guarantees two queen beds, confirm Saturday morning luggage storage before check-in, and check the room's noise-facing location request. The printmaking spaces and aquarium tickets also remain unreserved.
